_about: Mock-interview questions keyed by a term in terms.json. Each point lists phrases that show the answer covered it (matched case-insensitively). star: true adds the STAR points below. {company} and {term} are filled in.

star_points.label: what you did, in first person

generic_tech.q: The posting asks for {term}. Walk me through a project where you used it: what you built, one decision you made, and how it turned out.

points.label: names {term} and what you built with it

company.q: Why {company}, and why this role in particular?

points.label: connects it to your own experience
what you want to learn or contribute

company.q: Tell me about yourself in under a minute, and tie it to this role at {company}.

points.label: a skill the posting asks for

Python.q: In Python, what's the difference between a list and a tuple, and when would you use a dictionary or a set instead?

Java.q: In Java, how do HashMap and TreeMap differ, and what happens when two keys have the same hash code?

C++.q: In C++, what problem do smart pointers solve, and when would you use unique_ptr versus shared_ptr?

JavaScript.q: Explain how JavaScript handles a slow network call without freezing the page.

TypeScript.q: What does TypeScript catch that plain JavaScript doesn't, and when would you use an interface versus a union type?

points.label: unions allow one of several types

React.q: In React, what makes a component re-render, and how would you stop a big list from re-rendering too often?

Node.js.q: How does Node.js serve thousands of requests on one thread, and what kind of work would block it?

points.label: move heavy work off the main thread

SQL.q: You have users and orders tables. How do you find the top 5 customers by total spend last month, and how would you make that query fast?

NoSQL.q: When would you pick a document database like MongoDB over a relational one, and what do you give up?

points.label: you give up joins or transactions

Redis.q: You put a cache in front of a slow database. What can go wrong, and how do you avoid serving stale data?

Kafka.q: A payment event gets delivered twice through a queue like Kafka. How do you make sure the customer is only charged once?

Spark.q: Your Spark job is slow because one key has far more data than the others. What's happening, and how do you fix it?

Data pipelines.q: Design a daily pipeline that loads app events into a warehouse. What happens when a run fails halfway?

Distributed systems.q: Your service runs on three servers and one dies in the middle of a request. What does the user see, and how do you design for it?

System design.q: How would you design a link shortener that handles millions of clicks a day?

Microservices.q: When would you split an app into microservices, and what new problems does that create?

APIs.q: Design the API for a to-do app. What endpoints would you create, and how do you handle errors and versions?

Data structures and algorithms.q: Given a list of numbers and a target, how do you find two numbers that add up to the target, and what's the time complexity?

points.label: use a hash map or set

Object-oriented design.q: How would you design the classes for a parking garage? Name the main objects and one design choice.

Concurrency.q: Two threads update the same bank balance at the same time. What can go wrong, and how do you prevent it?

Testing.q: How would you test code that charges a credit card without charging a real card?

CI/CD.q: Walk me through what should happen between a git push and that code running in production.

Git.q: You and a teammate edited the same file and git shows a merge conflict. What do you do?

Linux.q: A Linux server suddenly gets slow. What commands do you run first, and what are you looking for?

Docker.q: What problem does Docker solve, and what's the difference between an image and a container?

points.label: a container is a running instance

Kubernetes.q: What does Kubernetes do when a pod crashes, and how would you roll out a new version safely?

AWS.q: How would you host a small web app on AWS, and how would you keep the bill low?

Cloud.q: What changes when you move an app from your laptop to the cloud?

Security.q: How should a web app store user passwords, and what attacks does that protect against?

Networking.q: What happens, step by step, when you type a web address and hit enter?

Observability.q: Users report errors but your dashboards look fine. How do you find the problem?

Performance.q: A page that loaded in 1 second now takes 5. How do you find out why?

Machine learning.q: Your fraud model gets 99% accuracy but it's useless. How is that possible, and what would you measure instead?

Deep learning.q: Your neural network does great on training data and badly on new data. What's happening, and what would you try?

points.label: early stopping or a smaller model

LLMs.q: You're building a chatbot over a company's documents. How do you stop it from making things up?

NLP.q: How would you sort support tickets by topic when you start with zero labeled data?

Computer vision.q: How would you build a model that spots defects in product photos with only 200 labeled images?

Statistics.q: Explain a p-value to a non-technical manager, and one way people misuse it.

A/B testing.q: Your A/B test shows a new button lifts clicks by 2%. How do you decide whether to ship it?

Data analysis.q: Weekly active users dropped 10% last week. How would you figure out why?

points.label: check the data is right first

Data visualization.q: Design a dashboard for a manager who has 30 seconds a day. What goes on it and what stays off?

Excel.q: You get a messy spreadsheet of 5,000 transactions. How would you total spend by category and month in Excel?

Financial modeling.q: Walk me through how the three financial statements connect.

Accounting.q: What's the difference between accrual and cash accounting, and why does it matter?

Product sense.q: Pick an app you use every day. What's one thing you'd improve, and how would you know it worked?

Marketing.q: How would you get the first 1,000 students at a university to try a new app?

Project management.q: Your project is two weeks behind and the deadline can't move. What do you do?

Embedded systems.q: How would you debug a microcontroller that randomly resets in the field?

Hardware/circuits.q: How would you make sure a new chip feature works before it ships?

CAD.q: Walk me through a part you designed in CAD and one change you made after testing it.

Supply chain.q: A key supplier will be two weeks late. How do you keep production running?

Communication.q: Tell me about a time you explained something technical to someone who wasn't technical.

Collaboration.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate. What happened?

Ownership.q: Tell me about something you built or fixed that nobody asked you to.

Ambiguity.q: Tell me about a time the instructions were unclear. How did you move forward?

points.label: made an assumption and tested it

Learning quickly.q: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new tool or topic fast.

Problem solving.q: Tell me about the hardest bug you've fixed. How did you track it down?

Customer focus.q: Tell me about a time you changed your plan because of feedback from a user or customer.

Leadership.q: Tell me about a time you led a group without being the official leader.

points.label: how you got others on board
